unprovided_artwork_plan.title: Open- and short-circuit characteristics used to obtain synchronous impedance
unprovided_artwork_plan.alt: Recommended study diagram showing the open-circuit characteristic and short-circuit characteristic of a synchronous generator against field current, with the same field-current setting used to obtain open-circuit voltage and short-circuit current.
unprovided_artwork_plan.teaching_note: The two tests must be read together. Choose one field-current value, read the corresponding open-circuit voltage \(V_{OC}\) from the OCC and short-circuit current \(I_{SC}\) from the SCC, and use those matched readings to calculate \(Z_s=V_{OC}/I_{SC}\).
unprovided_artwork_plan.search_query: NPTEL Lecture 90 OC SC Test Synchronous Generator OCC SCC characteristics
unprovided_artwork_plan.ai_prompt: Create an NRS educational diagram for the synchronous-impedance (EMF) method using the verified OCC/SCC reference. Show field current on the horizontal axis and clearly distinguish the open-circuit voltage characteristic (OCC) from the short-circuit current characteristic (SCC). Mark one common field-current setting and show that the corresponding V_OC and I_SC readings are taken at that same excitation before forming Z_s = V_OC/I_SC. Do not invent numerical scales, machine ratings, connection details or test values. Preserve the qualitative curve shapes and labels from the chosen verified reference, and apply NRS blue-ink notebook styling only after semantic verification.

unprovided_artwork_plan.title: Magnetic locking of the DC-excited rotor field with the rotating stator field
unprovided_artwork_plan.alt: Recommended educational diagram showing a rotating stator magnetic field and a DC-excited rotor magnetic field locked together and rotating at synchronous speed.
unprovided_artwork_plan.teaching_note: Read the picture as two magnetic fields moving together. The stator field rotates at \(N_s\); once the DC-excited rotor field is locked with it, the rotor follows at the same speed. In steady synchronous operation there is therefore no relative speed between the two magnetic fields.
unprovided_artwork_plan.search_query: NPTEL Lecture 82 synchronous motor operation rotating magnetic field rotor locking
unprovided_artwork_plan.ai_prompt: Create an NRS educational schematic of the basic synchronous-motor operating principle using the verified NPTEL reference. Show a rotating stator magnetic field and a DC-excited rotor with clearly identified North and South poles. Show that, after magnetic locking, the rotor field and stator rotating field move together at the same synchronous speed N_s. Do not add numerical values, detailed phasors, starting arrangements, damper windings, torque-angle values or circuit details unless they are present in the verified reference. Keep the diagram limited to the R25 operating principle and use NRS blue-ink notebook styling after semantic verification.
unprovided_artwork_plan.caption: Magnetic locking in a synchronous motor
